Take this free CAT Mensuration 2D online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Mensuration (2-D) chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Mensuration (2-D) tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Mensuration (2-D)

Perimeter and area of rectangles, squares, triangles, circles and composite plane figures.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Rectangle: perimeter 2(l+b), area l·b.
  • Triangle: area ½·b·h or Heron’s √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)).
  • Circle: circumference 2πr, area πr².
  • Equilateral triangle area = (√3/4)a².

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing perimeter (units) with area (square units).
  • Using the wrong π value for the given data.
  • Forgetting to subtract cut-outs in composite figures.
